title: THE FIRSTBORN AND THE REDEMPTION PRICE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The first offspring of every womb belongs to me, including all the firstborn males of your livestock, whether from herd or flock. Redeem the firstborn donkey with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem all your firstborn sons. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.'" - Exod 34:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This looks strange to us until we remember what happened on the last night in Egypt. Every firstborn in the land was under judgement, and Israel's firstborn survived only because a lamb died and its blood marked the door.

So God says: the firstborn belongs to Me. They were not spared because they were better. They were spared because something died in their place. This ongoing practice was a permanent reminder of that.

Notice the donkey. An unclean animal, unfit for sacrifice, with no way to redeem itself. Either a lamb dies in its place, or judgement falls. There is no third option.

That is a stark picture, and it is our picture too. We cannot make ourselves acceptable. Either a substitute is provided or we bear the consequence ourselves. Peter says we were redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect (1 Pet 1:18-19).

"No one is to appear before me empty-handed" is also worth sitting with. Not because God needs our gifts, but because grasping what we have received naturally produces giving. Freely you have received, freely give (Matt 10:8).

We come to God today with full hands — holding out Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you grasp that you were bought at a price?
2. What does it mean that you had no way of redeeming yourself?
3. How does gratitude for redemption shape your generosity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, I was the donkey with no way out, and You were the Lamb. Thank You for redeeming me with Your own blood. Amen.
